name: Tokelau
summary: A dark blue field with a yellow Tokelauan canoe sailing toward the hoist and four white stars of the Southern Cross. Adopted in 2009, it was designed locally.
origin: Tokelau, three atolls administered by New Zealand, used the New Zealand flag. The General Fono (council) adopted its own flag on 7 September 2009, after earlier proposals.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The canoe; also the three atolls' coral sand.

symbols.name: Canoe (vaka)
symbols.description: A yellow Tokelauan canoe with sail.
symbols.meaning: Tokelau's journey toward self-determination, carried by the people.

symbols.name: Southern Cross
symbols.meaning: Navigation, and the guidance of the stars.

facts: Tokelau voted twice (2006 and 2007) on self-government in free association; both narrowly failed the required two-thirds.
Tokelau was among the first territories to be powered almost entirely by solar energy.
Its three atolls are Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo.
clues: Dark blue with a yellow canoe and four white stars.
Its canoe represents a journey toward self-determination.
Its three atolls voted twice on self-government.
